Invitation to Sociology: A Humanistic Perspective is a 1963 book about sociology by the sociologist Peter L. Berger , in which the author sets out the intellectual parameters and calling of the discipline of sociology.

Background

[ edit ]
Berger was a student of social scientist Alfred Schütz , and was influenced by Schütz's approach to sociology. [ 1 ]

Abstract
Although Peter L. Berger's "Invitation to Sociology" (1963) was published more than 25 years ago, it remains one of the most widely adopted, anthologized, and cited of the many introductory books in the field. Berger's book, however, has received surprisingly little critical attention since its publication. The purpose of this analysis is to reconsider the place of this classic work in teaching undergraduate sociology. Accordingly, this article charts the commercial success and the intellectual impact of Invitation, describes the image of sociology that it offers to newcomers to the field, reviews its treatment of human freedom as a sociological issue, evaluates its usefulness in pedagogy, and examines the vision of the world that it conveys to students.
